title: the birth of the cousins
hook: the three brothers grow up, the pale one is crowned, and a princess of Gandhara learns her husband is blind and ties a cloth over her own eyes
carry: a strip of cloth, folded and tied

segments.voice: Yesterday in the birth of the cousins: Pandu the pale, and Vidura, the maid's son, born because she met a stranger with respect — she simply showed him respect. Whom did you greet? Day seven hundred twenty-four.

A strip of cloth, folded over and over, tied behind the head. That's the image this part of the story leaves behind. A young princess named Gandhari, from the land of Gandhara, has been promised to a prince of the Kurus. Then she learns that he is blind. She takes a cloth, folds it, and binds her own eyes. Before we get to why, we need to see the boys grow up.
screen: `A CLOTH, FOLDED MANY TIMES.` → `A PROMISED PRINCESS.` → `SHE BINDS HER OWN EYES.`

segments.voice: With the three boys born, the text says, the land of the Kurus flourishes: rains on time, full harvests, cities busy and safe. Bhishma raises the princes as his own, and trains them. Each grows into a gift. Dhritarashtra, the text says, becomes the strongest. Pandu becomes the finest archer. And Vidura, the text says, has no equal in knowing dharma. Then comes the question of who rules. Dhritarashtra is the eldest. But he's blind, and the text says that's why he is passed over. Vidura is wise, but his mother was a servant, and so he's passed over too. The crown goes to Pandu, the younger. Hold on to that. Some readers find, in a firstborn watching his younger brother take the throne, a seed of much that follows. Now Bhishma looks for wives. He hears of Gandhari, daughter of the king of Gandhara, and asks for her for Dhritarashtra. Her family hesitates over a blind groom, then agrees. And when Gandhari hears, she binds her eyes, resolving, the text says, out of regard for her husband, never to have more than he has. Her brother, Shakuni, brings her to Hastinapura. Remember his name; he'll matter later. Readers take the blindfold more than one way. Some see a wife's complete devotion. Some see a woman refusing to be the one who sees in a marriage she didn't choose. Some see grief, worn on the face. The text gives the reason in her husband's honor, and leaves the rest of her silent. Two people who cannot see now sit beside the throne, one by birth and one by choice, and a pale king sits on it.
screen: `THE KURU LAND FLOURISHES.` · `THE CROWN GOES TO PANDU.` · `GANDHARI BINDS HER EYES.` · `SHAKUNI BRINGS HER HOME.`

segments.voice: If it's comfortable, close your eyes now, or let them rest low. Gandhari chose to share what her husband couldn't have. Sit for a moment without sight, and notice what fills the space: sounds, the feel of the floor, the air on the skin. Then bring to mind someone close to you who carries something you don't, a loss, an illness, a limit. You don't have to fix it. Just sit beside it, as she did, for a few breaths. The bell holds the time.
Gandhari, the princess who bound her own eyes, out of regard for the blind husband she married, Dhritarashtra.
Your line: a strip of cloth, folded and tied. Today, for one hour, go at the pace of someone close to you who can't go at yours. Day seven hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: In Hindu retellings Gandhari is remembered as a figure of pativrata, devotion to a husband, and the blindfold is the image tellers and painters use for her.

original.note: Sanskrit Gandhari: the princess of Gandhara, wife of Dhritarashtra, who bound her eyes.

trapdoor: what you thought: a woman who chose to be blind.
what it means: a bride who refused to see more than her husband could.
what a scholar hears: the crown passes over the eldest here, and the text has already named Shakuni.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (the Kuru land flourishes; the princes' gifts; Pandu crowned; Gandhari's marriage and blindfold; Shakuni)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: the prosperity of the Kuru land after the births; Dhritarashtra strongest, Pandu foremost archer, Vidura unequalled in dharma (these are the text's comparisons, kept as 'the text says'); Dhritarashtra passed over for blindness and Vidura for his birth; Gandhari's family's hesitation; her blindfold and its stated reason; Shakuni bringing her.
Gandhari's boon of sons from Shiva and their count are left out under the claims rule; tomorrow and day 727 can pick them up.
The three readings of the blindfold are unattributed and unranked.
howItsDone describes how Gandhari is remembered in retellings; confirm phrasing.
Kunti's and Madri's marriages to Pandu are left for the next day.
Editor pass: 'she doesn't weep, the text says' cut (not in the text); stock line 'every royal family dreads' and the 'seed of everything that follows' overclaim softened; garbled carry rewritten.
Audit pass: 'two blind people' changed, since Gandhari is blindfolded by choice, not born blind.
